title: US STOCKS-Wall St edges lower on tech retreat, trade concerns Reuters
text:
US STOCKS-Wall St edges lower on tech retreat, trade concerns (For a live blog on the U.S. stock market, click LIVE/ or type LIVE/ in a news window)
* Allergan (NYSE: AGN ) drops as 2019 forecast misses estimates
* Harley-Davidson tumbles on 4th-qtr profit miss
* 3M (NYSE: MMM ), defense companies lead industrial stocks higher
* Apple dips ahead of earnings
* Dow up 0.10 pct, S&P dips 0.30 pct, Nasdaq down 0.83 pct (Changes comment, adds details, updates prices)
By Sruthi Shankar
Jan 29 (Reuters) - The S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell on Tuesday, as technology stocks pulled back, while concerns about the upcoming U.S.-China trade talks and mixed earnings reports gave little impetus for markets to recover from a slide a day earlier.
Wall Street sold off on Monday as profit alerts from Caterpillar Inc (NYSE: CAT ) CAT.N and Nvidia Corp NVDA.O raised fears that a slowdown in China and tariffs could take a bigger hit on profits.
Industrial stocks .SPLRCI , which took a beating after Caterpillar's warning on Monday, gained ground. The index rose 1.1 percent, driven by strong reports for 3M Co MMM.N and defense companies, in turn helping the Dow Jones industrial index stay afloat.
Technology stocks .SPLRCT fell 0.9 percent with Apple Inc AAPL.O , set to report after market close on Tuesday, dipping 0.6 percent. Amazon.com Inc AMZN.O , Facebook Inc FB.O and Microsoft Corp MSFT.O , all scheduled to report later this week, fell more than 2 percent.
"Investors are trading with caution, like they normally do ahead of any big trade negotiation and a central bank event," said Everett Millman, precious metals specialist at Gainesville Coins in Lutz, Florida.
"There is a lot of mixed signals that is creating this no man's land where there is no clear direction and markets get into this trend of back and forth."
In a potential setback to the progress in U.S.-China trade talks, the Justice Department leveled charges against China's telecom giant Huawei HWT.UL days before a high-level meeting between the two countries in Washington, aimed to tackle a prolonged tariff war that has roiled financial markets. Federal Reserve begins its two-day monetary policy meeting on Tuesday. After raising rates gradually last year, the central bank is taking a wait-and-see approach to further tightening in the face of an overseas slowdown and market volatility. data also added to weak sentiment. Conference Board's consumer confidence index fell to its lowest since July 2017, with a reading of 120.2 in January, that fell short of analysts' estimate of 124.7. 11:21 a.m. ET the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI was up 23.95 points, or 0.10 percent, at 24,552.17, the S&P 500 .SPX was down 7.99 points, or 0.30 percent, at 2,635.86 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was down 59.09 points, or 0.83 percent, at 7,026.60.
Six of the 11 major S&P sectors were lower. The S&P communication services index .SPLRCL fell about 1 percent, dragged down by wireless carrier Verizon Communications Inc (NYSE: VZ ) VZ.N , which dipped 2.2 percent after missing quarterly revenue estimates. contractors L3 Technologies Inc LLL.N rose 7.6 percent and Harris Corp (NYSE: HRS ) HRS.N climbed 7.9 percent after topping quarterly earnings estimates.
Harley-Davidson Inc (NYSE: HOG ) HOG.N dropped 7 percent after the motorcycle maker reported a lower-than-expected quarterly profit, hit by declining sales in the United States. Plc AGN.N fell 7.5 percent after the Botox maker forecast 2019 revenue below expectations. issues outnumbered decliners for a 1.31-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. Declining issues outnumbered advancers for a 1.18-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P index recorded 10 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq recorded 19 new highs and 16 new lows.
